newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Poles face extradition over W.Africa ship killings.
newsitem.headline: Poles face extradition over W.Africa ship killings.

text.p: Germany and Poland are both planning to request extradition of two Poles detained in Ivory Coast for allegedly murdering two German ship officers off the coast of West Africa, according to Ivorian police sources.
Germany has requested the Poles be extradited to Bonn to face trial there because the victims and the vessel MV Jannah were German. But Polish officials say they will block this.
"If it comes to extradition, we will not let them be sent to Germany since they are Polish citizens," said Polish Charge d'Affaires Piotr M'Sliwiec.
The two Poles were detained last week after the Antigua-flagged vessel docked in Abidjan.

The ship's crew told police that Captain Claus-Herman Clausen and engineer Ulrich Birkelbach, both 50, were stabbed to death and their bodies tossed overboard as the ship sailed to Abidjan from Port Harcourt, Nigeria, on December 10.
Eleven other crew members overpowered the accused and handed them over to Ivorian police.
A police officer told Reuters the suspects might appear in court on Monday for an extradition hearing.
Port officials said the 4,455 gross tonne Jannah left Abidjan on Wednesday for Hamburg with 4,000 tonnes of cocoa and a cargo of timber.
